# Tobit Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** As they drew near to Kaserin, which is before Nineveh,

**11:2** Raphael said to Tobias, "You know how your father was when you left him.

**11:3** Let us go ahead of your wife and prepare the house while she is still on the way."

**11:4** They went on together, and Raphael said to him, "Take the gall in your hand." The dog ran along behind them.

**11:5** Anna was sitting and watching the road for her son.

**11:6** She saw him coming and called to his father, "Look — your son is coming, and the man who went with him!"

**11:7** Raphael said to Tobias before he drew near to his father, "I know that his eyes will be opened.

**11:8** Apply the fish gall to his eyes; the medicine will work and will dissolve the white films on his eyes, and your father will see the light."

**11:9** Anna ran and threw herself on her son's neck and said to him, "I have seen you, my child; now I can die." And she wept.

**11:10** Tobit rose and came stumbling out through the courtyard gate, and Tobias went toward him,

**11:11** carrying the gall in his hand. He breathed on it, then steadied his father and applied it to his eyes, saying, "Take heart, father."

**11:12** He put the medicine on, and it stung. Tobit rubbed his eyes with both hands, and the white films peeled away from the corners of his eyes.

**11:13** Tobit saw his son and fell on his neck and wept, saying, "I have seen you, my child — the light of my eyes!" And he blessed God

**11:14** and said: "Blessed are you, O God, and blessed is your name forever and ever, and blessed are all your holy angels.

**11:15** For you afflicted me, yet you have had mercy on me; and now I see my son Tobias!" His son went in rejoicing and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.

**11:16** Tobit went out to meet his daughter-in-law at the gate of Nineveh, rejoicing and blessing God. Those who saw him walking were astonished, and Tobit gave praise before them all, because God had shown him mercy.

**11:17** When Tobit drew near to Sarah his daughter-in-law, he blessed her and said, "Welcome, my daughter. Blessed is your God who has brought you to us, my daughter. Blessed is your father, and blessed is my son Tobias, and blessed are you, my daughter. Come in with joy to your house, with blessing and with joy. Come in, my daughter."

**11:18** There was joy on that day among all the Jews in Nineveh.

**11:19** Ahikar and Nadab, his kinsmen, came to rejoice with Tobit. The wedding feast of Tobias was celebrated with joy for seven days, and many gifts were given to him.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 11 is the narrative and emotional climax of Tobit. SOPHIA's deliberations focused on four critical moments: (1) Anna's watchful sitting (v. 5); (2) her reunion cry (v. 9); (3) the step-by-step healing sequence (vv. 10-12); and (4) Tobit's welcome to Sarah (v. 17).

LOGOS provides the base throughout. PNEUMA's contributions are adopted in v. 11 (the addition of "steadied his father" before applying the gall — this is plausibly implied by the context of a blind man and is dramatically significant) and in the treatment of the healing sequence's physicality in v. 12. EMET's "white-films" is adopted over the more generic rendering in other agents.

On verse 9: PNEUMA's "now I could die happy" adds "happy" which is not in the Greek. LOGOS's "now I can die in peace" adds "in peace" which is also not in the Greek. SOPHIA returns to the more literal "now I can die" — the phrase is itself a complete formula (it echoes Simeon's words in Luke 2:29 and Jacob's in Gen 46:30); it does not need a gloss to explain it.

On verse 17: The repetition of "my daughter" is preserved in full. PNEUMA reduces it slightly; SOPHIA follows LOGOS/EMET in preserving the anaphora.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA Resolution |
|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|-------------------|
| 11:4 | The dog | "the dog followed after them" | "the dog ran along behind them" | "the dog trotted along behind them" | "the dog ran along behind them" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's "trotted" adds characterization not in text |
| 11:5 | Anna's posture and activity | "Anna was sitting and looking down the-road" | "Anna was sitting and watching the road" | "Anna was sitting outside, watching the road, the way she always did" | "Anna was sitting and watching the road" — LOGOS; PNEUMA adds "outside" and "the way she always did" beyond text |
| 11:6 | Anna's announcement | "said to his-father" | "called to his father" | "jumped up and called to Tobit" | "called to his father" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's "jumped up" adds a physical action not in text |
| 11:8 | Medical term | "white-films" | "white films" | "film that covers them" | "white films" — LOGOS/EMET; preserves leukōmata as a meaningful medical descriptor |
| 11:9 | Anna's reunion cry | "from now on I can die" | "now I can die in peace" | "now I could die happy" | "now I can die" — returned to literal; the formula needs no gloss; cf. Gen 46:30, Luke 2:29 |
| 11:9 | Physical gesture | "fell on the neck-of her-son" | "threw herself on her son's neck" | "threw herself onto her son and held him" | "threw herself on her son's neck" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's "held him" adds detail beyond the Greek |
| 11:11 | Application of gall | "he blew-on-it and held-it and applied-it" | "he breathed on it, then took hold of his father and applied it" | "he breathed on it gently, and then — steadying his father — pressed it" | "breathed on it, then steadied his father and applied it" — SOPHIA conflation; "steadied" from PNEUMA adopted as contextually necessary |
| 11:12 | Peeling of films | "the white-films peeled-off from the corners" | "the white films peeled away from the corners" | "the white film came away — peeling off in pieces" | "the white films peeled away from the corners" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's addition of "in pieces" not in Greek |
| 11:13 | Tobit's first sight | "fell on his-neck and wept" | "fell on his neck and wept" | "grabbed him, held him, and wept" | "fell on his neck and wept" — EMET/LOGOS; epepesen epi ton trachēlon is a specific biblical embrace formula |
| 11:15 | "with my own eyes" | Not added | Not added | "with my own eyes" | Not added — PNEUMA's addition is interpretively reasonable but not in the Greek |
| 11:17 | Repetition of "my daughter" | Preserved (bare "daughter") | Preserved ("my daughter") | Slightly reduced | Preserved in full — LOGOS; the anaphoric repetition is the point |
| 11:18 | "all the Jews in Nineveh" | "all the Jews who were in Nineveh" | "all the Jews in Nineveh" | "every Jewish family in Nineveh" | "all the Jews in Nineveh" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's "every Jewish family" paraphrases |
